name: OrgAsm
author: Donald Cameron (T-Soft)

provenance.from: AMOSTools/Extensions, out of aminet dev/amos/amostools.i386-aros.lha -- held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/. Its author's README says the directory is "every AMOS extension I can find, cut down to just their token tables with the make_extensions.pl script", and names the ExoticA AMOS extensions wiki page as the list it works from.
provenance.redistribution: Not redistributed here as software: the file carries no code at all. It is a token table with the library stripped out from under it, kept for identification and detokenising.
provenance.note: ExoticA's AMOS extensions list places it at slot 20. Nothing here observes it in a program: the slot is the wiki's recommendation and no more.

notes: TABLE ONLY. This is an AMOSTools stub -- the hunk shell and the token table survive, both length fields read zero, there is no code, and every entry's two routine words are overwritten with `====`. So the NAMES, the parameter SPECS and, because an id is the byte offset of its entry, the IDS are the original library's; the behaviour is not here and the evidence tier cannot rise above `manual` until a real binary turns up. The reader is checked against CRAFT and MusiCRAFT, which are held both ways, and agrees with them entry for entry -- see parseAmosToolsTable in src/tokens/libtok.ts. Thirteen keywords, and the only extension here whose names are not AMOS-shaped at all: every one is written `f<opengui>`, `f<closegui>`, `f<wait>`, `f<waitport>`, `f<getimsg>`, `f<replyimsg>`, `f<gotoamos>`, `f<gotowb>`, `f<openlib_intuition>`, `f<openlib_gadtools>`, `f<closelib_intuition>`, `f<closelib_gadtools>`, `f<itemaddress>` -- angle brackets included, which is legal in a token table because the tokeniser matches the bytes rather than an identifier. All thirteen are functions returning an integer. A gadtools shell, and a DEMO: the wiki records no full release, and the same author is behind Liberator, which is on its missing-extensions list.
